A man inside an insulated metallic cage does not receive shock when the cage is highly charged. Explain. a.

The potential at each point inside cage is same as that of the cage itself so that there is no potential difference between the man and the highly charged cage. Thus, the man does not receive any electric shock.
b. Is it possible to charge a capacitor to any potential?

No, we cannot charge a capacitor to -any potential. It is limited by the dielectric strength of the medium between the 'two plates of the capacitor. If we apply the electric potential greater than its dielectric strength, its insulation will break and charges cannot be stored. So, we can charge a capacitor to a potential less than the dielectric strength of the insulator kept between the plates of capacitor.

a. State the principle of conservation of linear momentum. How does NevRon's third law of motion lead to the
principle of conservation of linear momentum?

Statement: The principle of the conservation of linear momentum is stated as; "the total linear momentum of a system remains constant if no external forces act on the system." Or it states that "the total linear momentum of the system remains same before and after collision if there is no external force applied." For example, when a bullet is fired in the forward direction, there is recoil of the rifle in the backward direction so that the total linear momentum before and after firing is zero and hence, conserve the momentum.
